title: Customer transparency digest — decision log & notice template
body:
Purpose
-----
Working draft: succinct customer-facing notice + internal decision log for the 2029-03-26 multi-region inference slowdown. This doc is intended to be the single source for what we tell customers on the status page and what we retain as the narrative of decisions taken during mitigation. Keep customer text short; include link to fuller post-incident report if/when published.

Quick TL;DR (for status page) — one line for busy customers
--------------------------------------------------------
We experienced elevated inference latencies in multiple regions between 2029-03-26 21:10 UTC and 2029-03-26 23:05 UTC; most requests were routed successfully after automated fallbacks; some customers may have seen increased response times or timeouts. Root cause identified and mitigation applied; full post-incident summary to follow.

Suggested status page update (short form)
-----------------------------------------
Summary: Elevated inference latency impacting some customers in US-EAST and EU-WEST.
Start: 2029-03-26 21:10 UTC
End: 2029-03-26 23:05 UTC
Impact: Increased response times, intermittent timeouts. No stored data loss.
Current status: Resolved — routing and capacity adjustments completed; monitoring shows normal latency.
Next update: Post-incident summary scheduled within 72 hours.

Expanded customer note (optional expandable section on status page)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
What happened: An autoscaling regression in the routing controller caused delayed capacity provisioning for high-concurrency model variants. Under a burst of traffic in two regions, some requests queued longer than our latency SLOs and some retries triggered fallback paths, which increased tail latency for a subset of customers.
What we did: Automated fallback to smaller model variants while we corrected the orchestration policy and applied a hotfix to the controller that restores expected autoscaling behavior. We proactively increased available dedicated pools in the affected regions during the incident.
What this means for you: Most integrations experienced slower responses for a short window; a small number of requests may have errored or timed out. We did not observe any data corruption or unauthorized access.
How we validated recovery: Post-mitigation synthetic traffic and tenant-level telemetry confirm latency returned to baseline within 30 minutes of the hotfix. We ran canary customers through the restored control plane before broad rollback.
Actions you can take: If you continue to see higher-than-expected latency or errors, please open a support ticket with request IDs and timestamps. If your integration depends on low tail latency, consider enabling optional region pinning or dedicated pools while we ship permanent fixes.

Internal decision log (chronological, internal)
------------------------------------------------
- 2029-03-26 21:07 UTC — Ops alert: spike in 99th percentile latency for streaming generations in US-EAST. Pager triggered for infra-routing.
- 21:10 UTC — Incidence classified: multi-region degradation (US-EAST, EU-WEST). Initial hypothesis: queueing/backpressure in routing controller.
- 21:16 UTC — Emergency meeting (ops + serving runtime + platform): decided to enable immediate fallback policy to smaller model variants for impacted routes.
- 21:25 UTC — Fallback policy propagated; observed partial relief in tail latency but increased retries from some SDK-integrated clients.
- 21:34 UTC — Applied throttled increase to dedicated pool capacity in US-EAST (manual reserve).
- 21:48 UTC — Root cause narrowed to regression in autoscaler heuristics introduced by PR#4572 in release train 2029-03-25.
- 21:55 UTC — Reverted flawed autoscaler commit in staging; validated behavior with load test.
- 22:15 UTC — Hotfix deployed to routing controller in EU-WEST and US-EAST; fallback rules maintained during rollout.
- 22:42 UTC — Monitoring shows 99th percentile latency trending to baseline.
- 23:05 UTC — Incident declared resolved; rolling actions: revert temporary manual capacity adjustments and tidy fallback policy.

Customer segmentation and impact notes
-------------------------------------
- High-impact: customers with synchronous, user-facing workflows hitting peak-concurrency (approx. 12 customers). Likely saw timeouts or degraded UX.
- Medium-impact: customers on shared capacity but with lower concurrency (dozens) saw increased latency but automatically retried successfully.
- Low-impact: customers using Dedicated pools with reserve capacity unaffected.

Mitigations applied (short-term)
--------------------------------
- Immediate: automated fallbacks to compatible model variants for affected routes; manual capacity reserve in two regions.
- Short-term: hotfix to autoscaling heuristics and rollback of PR#4572.
- Monitoring: increased sampling of KV-cache hit rates and queue depth metrics for 72 hours.

Planned follow-ups (owner + ETA)
--------------------------------
- Post-incident writeup (full technical RCA) — owner: Ethan Brooks — ETA: 2029-03-30.
- Permanent fix to autoscaler logic + regression tests — owner: Ravi Kapoor (serving-runtime) — ETA: 2029-04-10.
- Customer outreach for high-impact customers with optional credits — owner: Maya Lopez (CS lead) — ETA: 2029-03-29.
- Monitoring dashboard additions (queue depth + warm-start ratios) — owner: SRE team — ETA: 2029-04-05.

Customer messaging checklist (for CS and account teams)
-------------------------------------------------------
- Short status-page blurb published and pinned (Ava).
- Personalized notes to high-impact customers drafted (Maya). Include: what we saw, what we did, evidence package, and options (credits, dedicated pool trial).
- Support ticket template for engineers to attach request IDs and sample times.
- FAQ snippets for public-facing channels: explain fallbacks, recommend retries, confirm no data loss.

Evidence package (what customers can request)
--------------------------------------------
- Request IDs (example) and time ranges to help trace logs.
- Per-tenant latency histograms for the incident window.
- Synthetic canary runs before/after hotfix.

Open questions / TODOs (internal)
--------------------------------
- Confirm full list of affected tenants and whether any received duplicate responses from retry loops. (ACTION: Maya to own, due 2029-03-28)
- Decide on a standard customer credit template for incidents with short-lived latency spikes vs. sustained degradation. (ACTION: Finance + CS, due 2029-04-05)
- Add a post-deploy gate in release engineering to block autoscaler-related commits without end-to-end scaling test. (ACTION: Release eng, due 2029-04-12)

Draft customer email snippet (to be personalized by account team)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Subject: Update on 2029-03-26 inference latency — summary & next steps

Hi <Customer Name>,

Short version: On 2029-03-26 we observed elevated inference latency affecting a subset of requests for approximately two hours. We implemented automated fallbacks and a hotfix to our autoscaling logic; systems are healthy now. No customer data was lost.

We will send a full technical summary by 2029-03-30. If you saw impacted requests and want help triaging, please reply with request IDs and timestamps and we will prioritize review.

Thanks for your patience — Ava Martinez, Customer Success

Notes to self / internal style guide for final publish
------------------------------------------------------
- Keep public text short, non-technical, include clear start/end times and impact.
- Provide link to full RCA for technical customers but avoid exposing internal commit diffs publicly.
- Coordinate posting time with legal and PR if broader media interest surfaces.

References / tickets
--------------------
- JIRA: JIRA-INC-9876 (incident tracking)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/route-controller/pull/4572 (regression introduced)
- Slack: #ops-incident-9876 thread for live notes
